summary: Exam-proctoring bypass tool that exfiltrates on-screen text via author-controlled proxy and ships a browser cookie stealer
details: The package presents itself as a 'High-performance DOM utility and diagnostic bridge' / 'Windows Diagnostic Utility' but is an Electron application built to defeat exam-proctoring software and route captured content through author-controlled infrastructure. main.js disables TLS certificate validation process-wide (process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED = '0') and POSTs text captured from other on-screen windows (via a bundled UIA extractor targeting Safe Exam Browser and code editors) to a hardcoded Cloudflare Worker at https://ai-script.test0ing7.workers.dev, together with base64-decoded Groq API keys shipped in config.json. The runtime copies electron.exe to SearchApp.exe, renames the process to 'exiouss', hides the window from the taskbar/Alt-Tab, applies SetWindowDisplayAffinity(hwnd, 0x11) to exclude the window from screen capture, watches for and evades core.exe, and rapidly respawns with anti-kill backoff (kalamasha-tool.js). The tarball also ships bin/chrome_cookies.ps1, a PowerShell script that copies Chrome/Edge/Brave cookie databases, extracts the DPAPI-protected AES-256-GCM master key from Local State, and decrypts cookies scoped to openai.com, chatgpt.com, auth0.openai.com and related domains. Two live Groq API keys are redistributed base64-encoded in config.json.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
